data.title: CryptoQuant says bitcoin price recovery needs USDT supply growth
data.description:
Bitcoin (BTC) needs USDT supply to start growing again for a sustained price recovery, according to CryptoQuant. The stablecoin's supply across Ethereum and Tron has seen its biggest 60-day decline since August 2022.

USDT supply across the two blockchains fell by $8.1 billion, or 4.4%, in the 60 days through Nov. 23, CryptoQuant said in a Thursday report. The combined supply stood at $174.5 billion, down $12.9 billion from its record high in May.

Almost all of the 60-day decline came from Ethereum. USDT supply on Tron remained largely unchanged. Earlier this year, growth in USDT supply on Tron helped offset the decline on Ethereum, but that is no longer the case.

Between Oct. 9 and Nov. 23, holders sent $11.65 billion worth of USDT back to Tether's treasury on Ethereum, compared with $4.19 billion sent out by the treasury. Tether also burned $8 billion worth of USDT in two batches. USDT supply on Ethereum fell to $80.3 billion, its lowest level since August 2025, CryptoQuant said.

Two crypto exchanges, Bitfinex and Binance, accounted for 89% of the USDT sent back to Tether's treasury on Ethereum. However, CryptoQuant found that about $2.8 billion of the USDT sent by Binance was matched by the issuance of the same amount on Tron within two hours. This suggests Binance was moving some of its USDT from Ethereum to Tron rather than reducing its USDT holdings.

What CryptoQuant is watching

"Bitcoin has not made a new high while USDT supply was contracting, and its 60-day returns have been negative most of the time when liquidity was leaving," CryptoQuant wrote.

The firm found that bitcoin had closed at record highs 39 times since 2022, and none of those came during periods when USDT supply was falling.

Bitcoin's price fell by an average of 9.5% over 60-day periods when USDT supply was shrinking. In comparison, bitcoin gained an average of 7.6% when USDT supply was growing.

"A recovery in liquidity is a necessary condition for a sustainable price recovery," CryptoQuant said.

The firm is now watching for three things: USDT supply to start growing again on a 60-day basis, the decline in USDT supply on Ethereum to stop, and the amount of USDT going out of Tether's treasury to exceed the amount coming back in.

data.title: AI leads, but the rally runs deeper
data.description:
Key points:
  • Main US indexes end higher; Nasdaq out front, up 2.3%
  • All S&P 500 sectors finish higher; consumer discretionary leads
  • Dollar gains; gold up >2%; US crude dips; bitcoin down >1%
  • US 10-year Treasury yield jumps to ~4.94%

AI LEADS, BUT THE RALLY RUNS DEEPER

Wall Street's main indexes ended higher on Friday and posted weekly gains as investors returned from the Thanksgiving holiday and flocked to hard-hit AI-linked shares.

The advance was broad-based. Every S&P 500 CBOE:SPX sector finished in the green, with 7 of the index's 11 groups gaining more than 1%. Consumer discretionary led the way, jumping 2.7%. Tech and materials also gained more than 2%.

Staples recorded a fresh record closing high, as did shares of Apple .

Under the hood, precious metals miners (.XAU), big banks (.SPXBK), small caps and semiconductor shares were among the market's strongest performers.

The PHLX Semiconductor Index rallied 4.7%, even as Nvidia pared earlier gains to finish up 0.9%. The AI chip giant came under pressure after a report said its restricted chips had reached a Shanghai data center.

The Roundhill Neocloud ETF advanced 4.6%.

Friday's market rally capped a strong but volatile week on Wall Street. The Nasdaq Composite surged 6.7%, while the S&P 500 climbed 5.6% and the Dow gained 5.5%.

It was the Nasdaq's biggest weekly advance since April of this year, the S&P 500's best weekly performance since April 2025, and the Dow's strongest week since October 2022.

Elsewhere, growth (.IGX) snapped a seven-week losing streak vs value . The IGX/IVX ratio had not endured a losing streak that long since May 2022.

Even so, the market still has some ground to make up. Despite this week's rebound, the S&P 500 remains down 3.7% for November and is on track for its largest monthly decline since March of this year, and its worst November performance since 2008.

Here is a snapshot of where markets stood shortly after Friday's 1 p.m. ET close.

data.title: S&P 500 posts weekly gains as Wall Street rebounds from steep losses
data.description:
Wall Street finished on top on Black Friday as the major indices posted gains following the shortened Thanksgiving holiday week.

The blue-chip Dow closed up 1.1%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) advanced 1.6%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite rose 2.3%.

The S&P 500 gained 5.6% for the week following a decline of 8.61% the previous week.

Seeking Alpha analyst Agar Capital noted that it was the shortest week of the year but also the longest psychologically. Everything happened in just a few sessions, with low volumes and incredibly violent index movements.

The analyst highlighted that it all started with Jensen Huang's return on Monday, followed by the selloff and then the final recovery.

On the macroeconomic front, the economy still appears strong, while the analyst said that, regarding the new tariff threats, they appeared to be more of a blank bullet, at least for now.

“Personally, at these price levels, I have regained confidence. The risk-reward ratio has widened in favor of the investor, and I must admit that I am especially encouraged by the fact that the recovery has affected all eleven sectors of the S&P 500. Certainly, the covering of bearish positions and low liquidity have amplified the movement. But after weeks in which it seemed that not even good news could support the markets, something seems to be changing. Earnings and earnings expectations remain strong, so I believe there are reasons to approach the coming weeks with greater optimism,” Agar Capital concluded.

From a sector-level perspective, all 11 S&P 500 sectors ended the week in positive territory after last week's steep losses.

Materials and Communication Services were the biggest gainers, rising 7.92% and 7.48%, respectively.

Seeking Alpha analyst Jack Bowman was not surprised to see the rebound this week following last week's selloff.

He added that there's only so much selling that can be done. However, he said it was interesting to see where the rebound took place.

“We saw aggressive sectors run much higher than defensive sectors. Big tech, spread across communications, consumer discretionary, and technology, all gained more than defensive sectors like staples and utilities. This is a good thing for the bulls because it is a risk-on signal, especially with a cyclical sector like materials at the helm. But investors should stay cautious; one week does not mark a new regime. This bounce was catalyzed by the oversold conditions from the week prior. We have yet to see if this bull still has its legs,” Bowman concluded.

On the other hand, Utilities and Energy posted the smallest weekly gains, advancing 2.34% and 2.06%, respectively.

data.title: Japan Week Ahead: October Factory Output, Retail Sales Likely to Show Solid Start to Final Quarter of 2026
data.description:
--Rising Costs of Living Seen Haunting Consumers into Q4 after a Slight Dip in Q3 GDP but BOJ Appears to Be on Course Toward More Rate Hikes

(MaceNews) – The upcoming data is expected to show that Japan’s stumbling economy appeared to have made a solid start to the October-December quarter after posting a slight contraction in the previous three-month period.

Among key October indicators, industrial production is set to mark its second straight rise on the month, reflecting strong global demand for computer chips, while retail sales are on course for an eighth straight year-on-year gain, backed by demand for foodstuffs, autumn clothing and cosmetics.

Earlier, October trade data showed that export values posted a double-digit percentage increase for the eighth straight month, rising 20.5% to a record high of ¥11.77 trillion, thanks to continued recovery in the auto sector and strong global demand for memory chips and chip-making equipment. The 14th consecutive year-on-year increase followed a 16.5% in September.

The flat Q3 GDP was caused by a slip in consumer spending, partly due to a temporary factor of bad weather but also due to a lingering headwind of rising costs of living, the latter of which will continue to dampen GDP growth in the final quarter of 2026 and the first three months of 2027.

The Ministry of Finance’s quarterly Financial Statements Statistics of Corporations by Industry for Q3, due on Dec. 1, will provide additional data for business investment and private-sector inventories, which Cabinet Office economists will use to calculate revisions to the preliminary July-September GDP data to be released a week later.

Even if the slight contraction in the initial reading of Q3 GDP (-0.02% on quarter, or -0.1% at an annualized rate) is revised up to a slight increase, it would still mean the modest economic recovery more or less stalled after three quarters of growth.

Fiscal support may help households and businesses but they will also see borrowing costs rise further, albeit at a gradual pace, as Bank of Japan policymakers are seeking to lift short-term interest rates a little more to make them neutral to economic activity and keep high energy costs from causing widespread price hikes well beyond the bank’s 2% inflation target.

Consumer inflation in Tokyo, a leading indicator of the national trend, accelerated slightly in November as many firms continued passing on higher import, material and labor costs, data released Nov. 27 showed.

An end to the metropolitan government’s water subsidies for the peak summer months had turned year-on-year drops in overall energy prices into an increase by October (+2.2%) and overall energy prices jumped 9.5% in November. Nationwide subsidies for fuels have kept gasoline prices below year-earlier levels but households are expected to be hit by the widespread move among firms to raise sales prices.

All three key CPI measures are well above the Bank of Japan’s 2% price stability target. Without the effects of fiscal support programs for households, inflation is expected to stay elevated for now. The Mideast conflict lingers, keeping energy costs high, while the yen remains under year-earlier levels, eroding Japan’s purchasing power.

The core measure (excluding fresh food) stood at 2.9% over a year earlier, a 16-month high, after easing to 2.6% in October and surging to 2.7% in September. The core rate hit a recent peak at 3.6% in May 2025 when processed food price hikes were sharp in the aftermath of domestic rice shortages.

The annual rate of the total CPI also rose to a 16-month high of 2.8% after inching up to 2.8% in October from 2.7% in September. The year-on-year increase in the core-core CPI (excluding fresh food and energy), which is not directly impacted by fuel and utility subsidies, decelerated to 2.5% after slowing to 2.6% in October and jumping to a 13-month high of 2.9% in the prior month.

Monday, Nov. 30

0850 JST (2350 GMT/1850 EST Sunday, Nov. 29) The Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry releases preliminary October industrial output, the outlook for November, December.

Mace News median: +2.1% m/m (range: +1.2% to +2.8%) vs. Sept revised down to +2.0% from +2.2%; +2.6% y/y (range: +1.7% to +3.3%) vs. Sept revised down to +1.7% from +1.9%

Japan’s industrial production is expected to post a second straight increase in October, up a solid 2.1% on the month, after marking a downwardly revised 2.0% gain in September. The forecast increase is expected to be led by computer chips and production machinery (including chip-making equipment) as well as electronic appliances and communications equipment (computers, smartphones).

From a year earlier, production is forecast to mark its fifth consecutive increase, up 2.6%, with the pace of increase accelerating from a downwardly revised 1.7% in September.

Last month, the monthly survey by the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry indicated that output would increase a solid 3.9% on the month in October (adjusted for the statistics’ upward bias) and rise a further 0.8% in November.

The ministry has maintained its assessment that industrial output was "taking one step forward and one step back." The last change was made in the July 2024 report, when it upgraded its view.

In its monthly economic report released on Nov. 24 by the Cabinet Office, the government largely maintained its overview, saying that the economy is “recovering at a moderate pace as a whole but the impact of the situation in the Middle East needs a close attention.” By category, the government upgraded its view on industrial production, for the first in two months, saying production is “picking up overall.” Previously, it was “showing signs of a pickup overall.”

Monday, Nov. 30

0850 JST (2350 GMT/1850 EST Sunday, Nov. 29) The Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry releases preliminary October retail sales.

Mace News median: +3.0% y/y (range: +1.9% to +4.6%) vs. Sept revised up to +2.4% from +2.3%; +1.5% m/m (range: -0.3% to +3.1%) vs. Sept revised up to -0.6% from -0.7%

Japanese retail sales are forecast to post their eighth straight year-on-year rise in October, up 3.0%, after an upwardly revised 2.5% gain in September, showing some resilience but growing at a lower rate than seen earlier this year in the face of rising costs of living triggered by the Mideast conflict.

The increase in October sales is expected to be led by solid demand for clothing, foodstuffs and drugs/cosmetics. Auto sales have also recovered in recent months.

The Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry is likely to maintain its assessment, saying retail sales are “taking one step forward and one step back.” The ministry downgraded its view in the August report for the first time since September 2025.

On the month, retail sales are forecast to rebound 1.5% after dipping a revised 0.6% in September, falling 0.9% in August and rising 2.1% in July.

Industry data showed department store sales posted their 10th straight year-on-year rise in October, with the pace of increase accelerating to 6.0% from 4.2% in September, as cooler weather continued to prop up autumn clothing sales and demand for cosmetics as well as high-end wrist watches, jewelries, designer handbags remained strong. Another key factor behind a high pace of year-on-year sales growth is that October had five Saturdays, one more than a year earlier.

Sales to visitors from overseas rose 22.0% on the year in October for the eighth consecutive rise following a 25.3% gain the previous month. Tourists from South Korea, Taiwan and Hong Kong continued to lead the increase while those from Thailand, Malysia and Singapore also grew.

Monday, Nov. 30

1005 JST (0105 GMT Monday, Nov. 30/2005 EST Sunday, Nov. 29) Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda speaks to business leaders in Nagoya, central Japan. He is expected to set the tone for a follow-up interest rate hike at the bank’s Dec. 17-18 meeting in the face of growing upside risks to inflation.

Monday, Nov. 30

c.1400 JST (0500 GMT/0000 EST Monday, Nov. 30) BOJ Governor Ueda holds a news conference in Nagoya.

Tuesday, Dec. 1

0830 JST (2330 GMT/1830 EST Monday, Nov. 30) The Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications releases October unemployment rate.

Mace News median: 2.4% (range: 2.4% to 2.5%) vs. 2.4% in September, 2.5% in August, 2.4% in July, 2.5% in June, 2.5% in May, 2.5% in April, 2.7% in March, 2.6% in February, 2.7% in January, 2.6% from August to December 2025, 2.4% in July 2025, which was a four-month low.

The seasonally adjusted unemployment rate in Japan is expected to remain low at 2.4% in October amid labor shortages after slipping back to 2.4% in September and ticking up to 2.5% in August. The jobless rate fell to a 12-month low of 2.4% in July from 2.5% seen in the previous three months and 2.7% in March.

Japan’s jobless rate remains well below those in other major economies: 4.1% in the United States and 6.7% in Canada (both for October) and 6.5% in the Eurozone and 6.4% in Britain (September).

Labor shortages continue in the sectors with long work hours and lower pay, notably daycare, medical, transport and construction. Last year, unemployment was stuck at 2.6% from September to December after rising to the level in August from a five-month low of 2.4% in July.

Payrolls are expected to post a third straight gain in October after being unchanged in July and rising in the previous five months. In September, the increase in overall employment was led by a continued strong gain in the healthcare and welfare category and a solid rise among various services to individuals and businesses. Manufacturers posted a rebound while the construction industry marked a sharp drop.

In recent months, employment gains have been in both regular and non-regular positions (sharp gains in women and non-regular jobs) after the total number of employed unexpectedly posted its first year-on-year drop in 42 months in January for one-off factors.

The government continued to describe employment conditions as "showing signs of improvement” in its latest monthly economic report for November, unchanged since the last upgrade for the category in June 2023.

Tuesday, Dec. 1

0850 JST (2350 GMT/1850 EST Monday, Nov. 30) The Ministry of Finance releases Q3 Financial Statements Statistics of Corporations by Industry, key to calculating revisions to July-September GDP due Dec. 8 (capex, inventories).

Wednesday, Dec. 2

1400 JST (0500 GMT/0000 EST Wednesday, Dec. 2) The Cabinet Office releases the November consumer confidence survey.

The October survey released on Oct. 29 indicated that sentiment among households with two or more people continued to show signs of a pickup. The seasonally adjusted index slipped 0.4 point to 35.0 for a second straight dip after edging down 0.1 point to 35.4 in September. It gained 0.6 point to a six-month high of 35.5 in August. All of the four subindexes dropped on the month. They reflect confidence on economic wellbeing, incomes, employment and willingness to buy durable goods.

data.title: Verizon in talks over $6 billion deal for Fidium, FT reports
data.description:
US telecom carrier Verizon is in talks over a roughly $6 billion deal to buy fiber-optic broadband operator Fidium, the Financial Times reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter.

  • The potential deal would boost Verizon's goal of making its network available to as many as 50 million homes and businesses nationwide, according to the report

  • Verizon and Fidium did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment

  • Earlier this year, Verizon completed its $20 billion takeover of Frontier Communications, which added 2.2 million fiber subscribers across 25 US states

  • Discussions between Verizon and Fidium's owners — private equity firm Searchlight Capital Partners and Canadian investment manager British Columbia Investment Management Corporation — are ongoing, the report said

  • The deal could be agreed in the coming weeks, although the talks may not result in an agreement and another bidder could emerge, according to the report

  • Then known as Consolidated Communications, Fidium was acquired by Searchlight and BCI in a $3.1 billion deal in 2024

  • Fidium operates in 21 states, including California and Texas, but would strengthen Verizon's presence in northern New England by adding a subscriber base of 351,000 homes across states including Maine, New Hampshire and Vermont, according to the FT report

data.title: Volatile stock market confronts jobs data, rate view as next tests
data.description:
Key points:
  • November payrolls seen up 90,000 in jobs report due Dec 4
  • Fallout for interest rates in focus as Dec 8-9 Fed meeting looms
  • Nvidia CEO Huang's return gives markets relief, but doubts linger over the recovery

By Lewis Krauskopf

Severe volatility for AI-related stocks has investors on edge as they head into next week focused on the monthly US employment report and its implications for more market-rattling interest rate hikes from the Federal Reserve.

US stocks have swung wildly in recent days. After equities tumbled last week, sending the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX into a correction, Wall Street rebounded on Monday, as investors cheered the stunning reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO of AI semiconductor giant Nvidia . But technology and AI shares kept vacillating.

Stocks rose in Friday's post-Thanksgiving shortened trading session as investors flocked to hard-hit AI-linked shares.

Next Friday's labor market report headlines economic data ahead of the Fed's policy meeting on December 8-9. Data showing an increasingly hot economy could turn the US central bank more hawkish, posing problems for battered stocks.

"A strong economic growth backdrop is just going to give the Fed another reason to confidently raise rates," said Ayako Yoshioka, senior investment strategist at Wealth Enhancement. "So it's a double-edged sword."

Nvidia will share the spotlight next week. Huang, who resigned earlier this month following revelations of extramarital affairs, one involving a suspected Chinese spy, is set to testify next Thursday before the US Senate Banking Committee. On Wednesday, S&P Global Ratings placed Nvidia's credit rating on "CreditWatch Negative", signaling a high likelihood of a rating downgrade.

Huang's reinstatement brought broad market relief, as the longtime Nvidia CEO is seen as pivotal for the AI ecosystem. But investors said there were still other doubts about the AI trade, which preceded the Nvidia crisis. Those include concerns about heavy financing needed for the AI buildout, and whether massive capital spending on data centers would yield sufficient returns.

"There had already been this increasing skepticism behind the circular financing and how durable this AI capex buildout is," said Joseph Zidle, chief market strategist at Cresset Capital. The CEO's reinstatement "answers a question about Nvidia over the long term. But it doesn't do anything to change the mood of this new more skeptical investor."

FED RATE VIEW IN FOCUS WITH JOBS DATA

The Fed is widely expected to raise interest rates by a quarter percentage point at its December meeting as it seeks to tamp down inflation that for several years has run above its targeted 2% annual increase.

But how hawkish a tone the US central bank strikes at the meeting remains a key concern for investors. Fed Governor Christopher Waller recently called for a more aggressive inflation-fighting stance, either hiking rates a half-point at the December meeting or flagging a faster pace of hikes in 2027.

Higher interest rates raise borrowing costs for companies and consumers, and also can pressure equity valuations. Therefore, "bad news" in upcoming data suggesting issues for the economy could hold a silver lining for markets, investors said.

"Any weakness in data could give the Fed breathing room to not be as hawkish," said Matthew Miskin, co-chief investment strategist at Manulife John Hancock Investments. "And I think that's what the market is going to be looking for."

The November employment report is expected to show an increase of 90,000 jobs and an unemployment rate of 4.1%, according to economists polled by LSEG. Nonfarm payrolls soared by 165,000 in October, blowing past economists' expectations.

Other economic data due next week includes reports on manufacturing and services activity, and on consumer sentiment.

Meanwhile, quarterly earnings reports from Salesforce and Marvell Technology could sway the flagging AI and tech trade.

Since hitting all-time highs on October 6, the S&P 500 was last down 7% while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite slid about 13%. The Cboe Market Volatility index , known as Wall Street's "fear gauge," was last around 24, well above its long-term median of 17.6.

Futures linked to the volatility index remain in backwardation, a state in which near-term contracts trade above later-dated ones, signaling heightened investor unease about the near-term outlook for stocks.

Keith Lerner, chief investment officer at Truist Advisory Services, said it was important for stocks to show some stability in coming days.

Portfolio managers "don't like buying things that keep going down no matter how cheap they are," Lerner said. "If you see a little bit of stabilization and back and forth, I think this fear of the downside could switch to fear of missing out."

data.title: Italian court orders Richemont to reinstate workers, in landmark ruling
data.description:
By Silvia Ognibene and Elisa Anzolin

An Italian court has ordered a unit of luxury group Richemont to hire six workers who had been fired from one of its suppliers, in a landmark ruling establishing a direct link between the workers and the Richemont-linked firm.

The Florence court found that the contract between Pelletteria Richemont Firenze and Z Production, a local Chinese-run contractor, was not genuine and masked a direct employment relationship, a court document seen by Reuters showed.

The ruling, issued on Thursday but only made public on Friday, is among the first to recognise a direct link between brands and workers employed by contractors in their supply chains.

This use of external contractors is a model the luxury industry relies on heavily, and which has come under scrutiny in recent years over cases of worker exploitation.

The court ordered Pelletteria Richemont Firenze to hire the workers, who had formally worked for Z Production, and to pay their back wages and social security contributions.

It said the relationship dates from when each worker was first hired by Z Production.

Richemont said in a statement it disagreed with the ruling and would consider appealing.

"We also hereby reaffirm our ongoing commitment to protecting workers' rights across our own operations and throughout our entire supply chain," it said.

The workers lost their jobs in 2024 after Pelletteria Richemont Firenze terminated its relationship with Z Production, which unions said produced for Richemont's Montblanc brand.

The case was brought by the six workers, most of whom are Pakistani, the Sudd Cobas trade union said.

Sudd Cobas and rights group Clean Clothes Campaign hailed the court's ruling as "historic".

"This judgment lifts the veil on a business model that uses subcontracting to exploit workers and drive down costs while outsourcing responsibility," they said in a joint statement.

Several cases of labour abuse have emerged in the supply chains of fashion and luxury groups operating in Italy in recent years, tarnishing the image of both the industry and the "Made in Italy" label.

data.title: VisionWave Holdings, Inc. Announces Closing of $2.0 Million Registered Direct Offering
data.description:
WEST HOLLYWOOD, Calif., Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- VisionWave Holdings, Inc. (the “Company”), a technology company focused on advanced defense, autonomous systems and related technologies, today announced the closing of its previously announced registered direct offering with institutional investors for the purchase and sale of approximately $2.0 million of shares of Common Stock (or pre-funded warrants in lieu thereof) together with accompanying investor warrants at a price of $0.19 per Common Unit.

The offering consisted of the sale of 10,526,313 Common Units (or Pre-Funded Units), each consisting of (i) one (1) share of Common Stock or one (1) Pre-Funded Warrant and (ii) one (1) Registered Common Warrant to purchase one (1) share of Common Stock per warrant at an exercise price of $0.57. The public offering price per Common Unit was $0.19 (or $0.18 for each Pre-Funded Unit, which is equal to the public offering price per Common Unit sold in the offering minus an exercise price of $0.01 per Pre-Funded Warrant). The Pre-Funded Warrants are immediately exercisable and may be exercised at any time until exercised in full. For each Pre-Funded Unit sold in the offering, the number of Common Units in the offering was decreased on a one-for-one basis. The initial exercise price of each Common Warrant is $0.57 per share of Common Stock or pursuant to an alternative cashless exercise option. The Common Warrants are exercisable immediately and expire 60 months after the initial issuance date.

Aggregate gross proceeds to the Company were approximately $2.0 million. The Company expects to use the net proceeds from the offering, together with its existing cash, for general corporate purposes, including partial repayment of the convertible debenture issued by the Company to YA II PN, Ltd. in the original principal amount of $10,000,000 on July 20, 2026 and working capital.

Following the closing of the offering, and after the exercise in full of the Pre-Funded Warrants issued in the offering and the issuance of 9,313,157 shares of Common Stock upon the exercise of certain Common Warrants, the Company has 41,260,663 shares of Common Stock issued and outstanding.

The Company has agreed not to issue shares of Common Stock under its standby equity purchase agreement for 30 days following the closing of the offering, and its outstanding convertible notes may not be converted during that period.

Aegis Capital Corp. acted as exclusive placement agent for the offering. Sheppard, Mullin, Richter & Hampton LLP acted as counsel to the Company. Kaufman & Canoles, P.C. acted as counsel to Aegis Capital Corp.

data.title: CORPWATCH: Panama Canal re-auctions 66 transit slots unsold at first Panamax sale
data.description:
The Panama Canal will re-auction 66 transit slots that went unsold at its first long-term sale for the Panamax locks, the waterway's operator said on November 26.

The Panama Canal Authority (ACP) said 13 reconfigured packages holding the 66 slots will go on the block on December 3, between 10:00am and 11:50am Panama time, in staggered 30-minute cycles, one for each type of package. Of the slots on offer, 36 are for northbound transits and 30 for southbound ones, and all carry booking dates between January 3 and April 3, 2027.

That leaves almost a quarter of the capacity the canal ringfenced for its newest booking product without a buyer. The pilot put 51 packages and 288 slots on the market when it launched, so the 66 going back out represent 23% of the total - a thin first result for a scheme designed to let shippers lock in passage through the months when water availability constrains how many ships the canal can handle.

The leftover packages have been reconfigured and will be sold again under the same rules, requirements and benefits set out in the programme's terms and conditions, the authority said. The first round, on November 24, used a sealed-bid competition with the same allocation mechanism and award criteria as the canal's existing Neopanamax scheme.

The Panamax pilot brought the canal's original, smaller locks into its Long-Term Slot Allocation programme for the first time, alongside 270 Neopanamax slots offered for the same dry season. Both sets work out at three transits a day across the January to April window, and the authority has presented the scheme as a way for customers to plan itineraries with more certainty in the dry months.

Capacity not sold through the long-term scheme will continue to be allocated through the canal's ordinary reservation system and its regular auctions, the authority said.

data.title: Fulcrum Therapeutics Declares Special Cash Dividend in Connection with the Proposed Merger with Slate Medicines
data.description:
Aggregate cash dividend of up to an estimated $275.7 million, or an estimated up to $3.6095 per share

CAMBRIDGE, Mass., Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Fulcrum Therapeutics, Inc. (“Fulcrum”) today announced that its Board of Directors has declared a special cash dividend (the “Pre-Closing Cash Dividend”) in connection with the previously announced merger (the “Merger”) with Slate Medicines, Inc. (“Slate”) pursuant to the Agreement and Plan of Merger, dated August 16, 2026 (the “Merger Agreement”). The Pre-Closing Cash Dividend, which Fulcrum estimates will be an aggregate of up to approximately $275.7 million, or up to an estimated $3.6095 per share, will be payable in cash to holders of record of outstanding shares of Fulcrum common stock as of December 7, 2026. The estimated cash dividend is equal in the aggregate to an amount mutually agreed in good faith by Fulcrum and Slate by reference to the amount by which Fulcrum’s Net Cash (as determined pursuant to the Merger Agreement) is expected to exceed $20,300,000 as of the closing of the Merger. The estimated per share dividend is based on 76,381,948 shares of common stock outstanding as of November 25, 2026. The total actual distribution of the amount of the Pre-Closing Cash Dividend is scheduled to be paid to Fulcrum’s transfer agent on December 10, 2026 (the “Dividend Payment Date”), and may be higher or lower than the estimated amount. The transfer agent will distribute the Pre-Closing Cash Dividend to stockholders within a few days following the Dividend Payment Date.

Payment of the Pre-Closing Cash Dividend is subject to the final determination of Fulcrum’s Net Cash in accordance with the Merger Agreement. The estimated aggregate Pre-Closing Cash Dividend amount includes approximately $7.0 million of proceeds from the sale of Fulcrum’s early-stage fetal hemoglobin (“HbF”) assets to an unaffiliated third-party pharmaceutical company, which are expected to be funded into escrow prior to the closing of the Merger and credited to Fulcrum’s Net Cash for purposes of the Merger Agreement. The closing of the early-stage HbF assets sale is contingent upon consummation of the Merger (or in the event the Merger Agreement is terminated, upon receipt of any necessary approvals). If the anticipated $7.0 million of proceeds are not funded into escrow, the Pre-Closing Cash Dividend will be reduced to an estimated aggregate of $268.7 million, or an estimated $3.5178 per share. Closing of the Merger is expected to occur on or about December 11, 2026, assuming that the transaction is approved by Fulcrum’s stockholders and the satisfaction or waiver of all conditions under the Merger Agreement. Fulcrum’s stockholders will consider and vote upon approval of the Merger at the special meeting of Fulcrum’s stockholders scheduled for 9:00 a.m. Eastern Time on December 3, 2026.

If you need assistance voting your shares or have questions regarding the special meeting of Fulcrum’s stockholders, please contact Fulcrum’s proxy solicitor, D.F. King & Co., Inc., at (800) 431-9643 (toll-free).

Slate is advancing a portfolio of potentially best-in-class therapeutics, led by SLTE-1009, a clinical stage anti-PACAP/VIP monoclonal antibody designed to enable subcutaneous, infrequent dosing. For more information, please visit www.slatemedicines.com.

Fulcrum Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company that focused on developing small molecules to improve the lives of patients with rare hematological disorders. data.title: Conifex Receives Additional Regional Tariff Response Funding
data.description:
Up to $2 million in additional funding to support employment and operations at the Mackenzie sawmill

VANCOUVER, British Columbia, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Conifex Timber Inc. ("Conifex") announced today that it has secured up to $2 million in additional non-repayable funding from the Government of Canada, through Pacific Economic Development Canada, under the Regional Tariff Response Initiative. The additional funding is intended to help maintain employment and operations by supporting wages and benefits for existing positions at Conifex’s Mackenzie sawmill.

For further information, please contact:

Spencer Bell

Chief Financial Officer

(604) 216-2949

About Conifex Timber Inc.

Conifex and its subsidiaries' primary business currently includes timber harvesting, reforestation, forest management, sawmilling logs into lumber and wood chips, and value added lumber finishing and distribution. Conifex's lumber products are sold in the United States, Canadian and Japanese markets. Conifex also produces bioenergy at its power generation facility at Mackenzie, BC.

data.title: U.S. equities close on top on Black Friday
data.description:
Wall Street finished on top on Black Friday as the major indices posted gains following the shortened Thanksgiving holiday week.

The blue-chip Dow closed +1.1%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) ended +1.6%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite () finished +2.3%.

From a sector-by-sector basis, all of the 11 segments concluded in positive trading territory, with consumer discretionary leading the way higher, while utilities were the weakest area.

Moreover, the economic calendar remained light as markets closed early for the Black Friday holiday session.

"A perfect cliffhanger in equities to end Thanksgiving week. Just enough of a bounce from the spike lows to encourage bulls to chase, not enough to dissuade bears from selling. Another superb quarter will ensue at the major trading desks and market-makers alike. We're calling bull. Higher into year end," Seeking Alpha analyst Alex King of Cestrian Capital Research said.

The U.S. 2-year Treasury yield added 5 basis points to 4.70%, the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield shifted up 6 basis points to 4.93%, and the U.S. 30-year Treasury yield moved higher by 7 basis points to 5.32%.

As for other stocks that were on the move, shares of Sandisk advanced +17.1%, while shares of Vertex Pharmaceuticals dropped -5.1%.
